meta.title: Example Course
meta.description: A working example — copy this file's shape to add a real course.

questionBank.q: What is the capital of France?
questionBank.exp: Paris is the capital and most populous city of France.

questionBank.q: Which ocean is the largest by surface area?
questionBank.exp: The Pacific Ocean covers roughly a third of the Earth's surface.

questionBank.q: What is the capital of Japan?
questionBank.exp: Tokyo has been Japan's capital since 1868.

questionBank.q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
questionBank.exp: Abuja became Nigeria's capital in 1991, replacing Lagos.

questionBank.q: What does KYC stand for in banking compliance?
questionBank.exp: KYC (Know Your Customer) refers to the process of verifying a customer's identity to prevent fraud and money laundering.

questionBank.q: A non-performing loan (NPL) is generally one where repayments are overdue by at least how many days?
questionBank.exp: Under most regulatory frameworks, a loan is classified as non-performing once payments are 90+ days past due.

questionBank.case: ABC Bank reported a 40% rise in non-performing loans after relaxing its collateral requirements in Q1. Management argues the growth in loan volume more than compensates for the higher default rate.
questionBank.q: Which control weakness most directly explains the rise in defaults?
opts: Loosened collateral requirements without added credit assessment.
Rapid increase in overall loan volume during the quarter.
Management's optimistic view of loan growth versus risk.
A general rise in interest rates across the sector.
questionBank.exp: The relaxed collateral standard directly weakened the credit control that normally screens out higher-risk borrowers, which is why defaults rose — the other options describe consequences or context, not the underlying control failure.

questionBank.case: A regional bank's fraud team flagged a customer account receiving multiple small deposits from unrelated third parties, followed by a single large wire transfer out within 24 hours.
questionBank.q: What financial crime pattern does this most closely resemble?
opts: Structuring / smurfing to obscure the source of funds.
Simple identity theft of the account holder.
questionBank.exp: Multiple small unrelated deposits followed by rapid consolidation and outward transfer is a classic structuring pattern used to avoid reporting thresholds and obscure the origin of funds.
